title: Libyan Coast Guard Intercepts Boat of ~80 Migrants Before SOS Méditerranée's Ocean Viking Could Reach It
detail: SOS Méditerranée said its rescue ship Ocean Viking altered course on Thursday, September 18, 2026 toward a boat carrying approximately 80 migrants in the central Mediterranean after a Frontex-relayed distress call, but the Libyan Coast Guard intercepted the vessel and returned everyone aboard to Libya before the NGO ship could arrive — preventing their disembarkation at a place of safety. The Ocean Viking went on to rescue 23 people, including unaccompanied minors, elsewhere the same day. InfoMigrants reported that while overall Mediterranean sea arrivals to Europe were down roughly 40% through mid-September 2026 versus the same period in 2025, fatalities rose: the IOM recorded nearly 2,300 deaths or disappearances on Mediterranean crossings so far this year, up from around 2,000 over the equivalent period in 2025. The Libya Observer separately confirmed the ~80-person interception and return in a same-week report, without citing an exact departure point.

media.caption: SOS Méditerranée's Ocean Viking crew documents a Libyan Coast Guard interception of a ~80-person migrant boat in the central Mediterranean, Sep 18, 2026

confidenceReason: SOS Méditerranée's own on-scene account of the interception, reported directly by InfoMigrants, is independently corroborated by a separate Libya Observer report on the same ~80-person return; neither source gives a precise departure point or GPS position for the interception.
